Requirements

Fulfilment of the admin role on IRIS requires the following:
An account on IRIS with the user group Administrator with unrestricted access on the system
To have been trained by another member of the IRIS Admin Team or the Business Service Manager
To have completed the Service Desk Analyst training on Oxford Service Manager (OSM)
To have been added to the Safety Office IRIS Support Team group on OSM

Not included in this guide

Guidance on the use of tickets and tasks in OSM

Queries will come to you in one of two ways:
As tasks on OSM to be investigated and actioned
Via email, either personal or Safety Office mailbox. This is not the primary way of support queries coming to the team to process and this behaviour should be discouraged for future use when it occurs. Once received via email, a ticket will need to be created on OSM and processed from there.

Investigation of Requests

Queries that come into the IRIS Support Team via tasks on OSM, may include requests that need to be verified with safety contacts throughout the University e.g. a request to create a new department in NDM would need to be checked with one of the Area Safety Officers for Medical Science if the request did not come from them.

Times when this is appropriate will be highlighted in the guidance that follows.

Escalations

There are two avenues of escalation for requests that come in via OSM:
Escalation to the IRIS Product Ownership Group (POG) for discussion and decision
Escalation to the supplier EcoOnline

In both instances, tasks that require escalation should be done so initially to the Business Change Analyst.

Reassigning Incidents from one Department to another

Reporters of incidents are asked to assign each incident they log to a Department, Faculty or School where the incident took place. This is not always a clear-cut decision due to the complex nature of the University and the buildings and spaces it occupies. There are some situations where it can be easy to assign an incident to an incorrect department to process.

A user on the system can reassign incidents between departments only if they have permissions to view incidents that take place in both of these departments i.e. if an incident was assigned to the Maths Department but should have been assigned to the Physics Department, a user could only reassign this if they had permissions to view incidents in both the Maths and Physics Departments. This means that the likelihood is only Area or Divisional Safety Officers are likely to be able to reassign incidents within their divisions, and Departmental Safety Officers are likely to not be able to do this.

The All tables tab displays the full hierarchy of tables that are available to the user in the current application. This could be displayed as a very long page of tables for applications with a large number of data tables. 
Saved Searches will usually be displayed on the right hand side of the Spotlight search page providing easy access to re-run searches that have previously been set up and saved. 

Your Search Criteria
Select a table to begin a new search. 
Your Criteria (as shown below) will provide some fields as default options to define your required search criteria. 

Make as many selections as required – the default setting is to find records that match all of your criteria. It is possible to change this to find records that match any of your criteria by using the ‘Find records that match…’ selector from the top of the Criteria box. 
To add additional fields to the criteria area use the ‘Add custom criteria’ option. Tick as many additional fields as are required. 
Fields that are from a related table can also be used as search criteria by selecting the link at the bottom of the additional criteria pop-up below and navigating to the required table then ticking the field. 
When all required criteria has been entered, click on the Run Search button. 

Your Search Results
Your results will appear at the bottom of the page below Your criteria. 
The number of results found that match your criteria will be displayed in brackets. 
It is possible to refine your criteria further and then click ‘Re-run search’ to alter the results that are returned. 

A few key fields will be included as columns in your results by default. 
Use the ‘Add or Remove Column’s button to add additional fields into your results in the same way as adding criteria. This includes navigating to related tables. 
Use the ‘Reorder Columns’ button to change the order of the fields included in your results. 
It is possible to view a record in more detail by clicking into one of the rows from your results – an option to return to search results will be available from both the edit and summary pages. 

Download options
All searches will include the option to Print – select the ‘Print’ button from between your criteria and your results and then use the printer options to set up the page layout and other formatting options. 

The Download button will provide a choice of either PDF or CSV. 
Selecting PDF will allow for further Page Size and Orientation settings to be chosen. 

Saved Searches
All users have the ability to save searches that will be available to re-run under the users own account. 
To save a search, complete the criteria selection and update results with any additional columns and reordering that is required and then select the ‘Save search’ button from between the criteria and results area. 

Enter a name for the search and then click the Save button. 
The search will now be saved on the Spotlight search page to be re-run as required. 
The saved search will also be pinned to the application homepage by default – use the unpin option shown above to remove a saved search from the homepage quick links. 
Publishing Saved Searches
Nominated users can also have additional privileges to publish saved searches for all users to run. 
An additional tick box will be available under the Save search option providing the ability to ‘publish’ the search to the Spotlight page of saved Searches for all users of the current application. 
Permissions to be able to publish saved searches can be granted by contacting the Info Exchange Helpdesk on 01926 844211 or emailing helpdesk@alcumusgroup.com

Introduction

Exchange Administrators and other nominated key users who have been given ‘Create Reports’ access for an application are able to create and publish standard reports, aggregate the data and build a variety of graphical charts including Line, Bar, Pie using the aggregated results. 

These reports are then available for all users of the application to generate online using their own run-time criteria where applicable. 

The functionality is available on all deployments using our IE2 technology. 

Any queries relating to this functionality should be directed to the helpdesk on 01926 844211 or via e-mail helpdesk@alcumusgroup.com 

Creating a Report

All users of the Info Exchange application are able to run searches at any time using any field combinations. 

An Exchange Administrator also has the ability to create a report and edit the report to further aggregate the data and build graphical charts. 

Exchange Administrators can also allow other key users to be able to create reports without the need for full Administration access. This can be permitted on an application basis by updating the user’s profile in the appropriate application through the Administration > Applications tool. 

It is recommended that the number of users able to create reports is kept to a minimum to avoid excessive numbers of reports being created or existing reports being altered unnecessarily. 

To create a report, click the Reports tab, select the spanner icon in the top corner and choose the “Create new report” option. 

Give the report a title and select the primary table for the report and then click Continue.

Report Settings

The following settings can be applied to a report during the initial set up and then updated at any time afterwards. 

A description can be entered about the report that will appear in smaller text under the report name on the main reports page. 
Select an icon from the available options to represent the report on the main reports page.

Add the report into a group - “Other reports” is the default group.

Tick to “Ignore user’s permissions when running report” if this report contains high level data only (no specific details) and it is preferable for users to report on all records not just the ones they usually have permissions to access. 

Tick to “Show the report on the application homepage”. This will force the report name to appear on the application homepage in the Reports box as a hyperlink for all users. If this is not activated users will still have the ability to add it their homepage if they wish. 

Tick to “Show tabs in docked orientation” to present the layout of the finished report in a docked tab format of data tables and graphs rather than stacked below each other on a single page view. 

Tick the “Publish to other users” when the report is complete and is ready for other system users to access and run. 
Select the “Page size” to determine the number of records to show on each page of the report data table. 

Tick “Show Hyperlinks” to allow the first column of each record in the data table to be used as a hyperlink clicking through to the summary page of the record. 

Tick “Aggregated rows to expand” to allow reports with aggregation to display a chevron that will expand to display all individual rows that are included in the aggregated row. Please note that activating this option can increase the page load time of a report. 

Tick “Enable CSV download” to display the download csv option on a report – this will be disabled by default. 

Click Save to update the report with the chosen settings. 

Report Criteria

The Criteria tab of the report configuration is divided into 2 sections – Fixed and Runtime criteria. 

Fixed criteria can be set up by the report creator and will be locked into the report each time it is generated with only records that match the fixed criteria values being returned.

Runtime criteria are fields that can be applied to the report as an initial page for the user running the report to decide which criteria options to choose. The report will then return records that match the user’s specified criteria values. 

A combination of the 2 can be used e.g. fixed criteria of records with an “Open” Status plus a runtime criteria of a Date field so that each user running the report can vary the records retuned by the date range entered but only Open records will ever be returned in the results.

To apply either type of criteria click the “Add additional criteria” button and tick the required fields from the available fields as shown below and click Done. 

For fixed criteria, select the required values from the chosen fields and click Done. 

Note that fields from related tables can also be included as criteria – when selecting the required fields use the blue hyperlink at the bottom of the field selector box to select a field from a related table. 

An example might be to navigate up the table hierarchy to the Site table and then tick the Region field from the list of fields in the Sites. 

When all criteria have been applied, click the Save Changes button. 

Data Table – Adding & Removing Columns

The next tab in the report configuration is the Data table and this displays the columns of data for the records that are returned in the report results. 

To add or remove columns from the data table, click on the Edit Columns options on the right hand side and choose “Add or remove columns” from the menu. 

Tick or un-tick the fields that are required as columns in the data table. 

Fields from related tables can also be included by using the blue hyperlink at the bottom of the window and following the same process as described in the Criteria section to navigate to other tables and tick required fields. 

Data Table – Reorder Columns

When the required fields are displayed as columns, these can then be reordered into a preferred layout. 

Note that if aggregation is going to be applied to the data, the aggregation field must be the first column in the table. 

To reorder the fields, select the Edit Columns option again and choose the “Reorder columns” option from the menu. 

Drag and drop each field into the appropriate order and click Done when complete. 

Aggregation

To aggregate records together and produce counts of the aggregated data click the icon next to the No aggregation status on the right hand side. 

2 levels of aggregation are supported in the Data table. 

To aggregate by the field that is the first column in the data table tick the first Aggregate option. 

To aggregate at 2 levels by the fields that are the first and second columns in the data table tick the 2nd Aggregate option. 

Click Done to apply the aggregation to the data table. 

If the fields required for aggregation are not displayed as options in the Aggregation settings box, the columns in the data table need to be reordered to first and second column position. The aggregation settings box will automatically update with the new fields after the reorder has been applied. 

Selecting an aggregation option will then prompt a choice of including subtotal rows.

When aggregating by 2 fields there will be an option to include a 2nd table in the data table area that shows the total record count by the 2nd field in a separate table.

To set the aggregation values click Edit Columns on the right hand side and select “Set aggregation types” from the menu. 

Choose the appropriate option from the list available for each column in the data table. Count or Sum are the most commonly required options. Click Done to update the data table. 

Data Table - Column Visibility

Sometimes fields have to be included in the report data table as a column for purposes such as plotting the field on a graph or including the field in a report calculation but the report creator does not actually want to show this field on the data table as a column to the users running the report. 

Column visibility can be set on or off to display only the required fields on the data table. 

Click the Edit Columns button on the right hand side and select “Set column visibility” from the menu option.

Tick or un-tick the fields to set the visibility for each column and then click Done. 

Data Table – Editing Columns

Changes can be made to an individual column by clicking on a column heading to change the settings for the column. 

914400top

The label of the column name can be changed by un-ticking the Use default label box and typing a new Column Name into the box provided. 

The column can be set to visible or not by ticking or un-ticking the box.

The aggregation setting for this column can also be updated through this interface.

Click Done to apply any updates to the data table. 

Data Table – Calculations

Calculated columns can be added into the report. There are some pre-defined calculation options plus the ability to add custom calculations using any fields that are added into the data column (including non-visible fields).

To add a calculated column click the Edit Column button on the right hand side and select “Add calculated column” from the menu. 

The types of calculation available will depend on the data fields included in the report, e.g. the Year to date total will only be available if there is a date field in the report table. 

All of the options will present the user with some further options to complete before the calculated column is added to the report. The example below is the Rolling total calculation type:

The report creator must select a related field from the fields that are used in the report (including non-visible fields) to apply the calculation to and then enter the Number of months rolling. 

Click Done to update the report data table with the new calculated column. 

The option for Custom calculation is more complex are there is no pre-defined calculation that will be applied and the report creator must configure the calculation using C# language. 

The first stage of adding a custom calculation is to create a Name and Label for the calculated column and then choose the type of data that the column is going to display. 

The next stage is to declare the fields that are to be used in the calculation – these must be present in the report table but can be non-visible fields. 

The calculation expression is then entered into the Expression box in C#. 

The calculation must be tested before it can be saved. 

Click Save calculation to add the new column into the report data table. 
Graphs

Multiple graphs can be added to a report using the data available in the data table of the report. 

To add a new graph click the Add Graph option on the right hand side and type in a Graph title. 

Select the type of graph and further options will then appear depending on the type chosen.

Bar, Column & Line Graphs

The options available are very similar for bar, column and line graphs. 

Bar graphs display the bars horizontally across the page and Column graphs display the columns vertically up the page. 
 

Graph Style

The Graph Style options are Standard, Sub-divided or Stacked. 

Standard will display one bar, column or line in a single block colour. 

Sub-divided bars and columns break a single data field into different coloured segments representing the values of the field e.g. Risk field divided into High, Medium & Low. 

Stacked bars and columns stack multiple data fields onto each other in different coloured segments. 

Legend Position

Choose a legend position on the graph e.g. on the Left or Right, Top or Bottom. 

Fields 

Select the field or fields to be plotted on the graph by ticking the required boxes. 

Use the Colour column to choose a specific colour for the field. 

For Column and line reports choose whether the field should be plotted as a Column or a Line and then against which Y axis it should be displayed. 

Axis Range & Increment

Set preferences for the Axis range e.g. 0 to 100 if the data plotted is showing percentages. 

Choose a preferred Increment for the Axis e.g. increments of 100.

Column or Line graphs provide options for both Y1 and a Y2 axis. 

Target Line

Add a target line onto the graph and set the value and colour of the line. 
Multiple target lines can be added. 

Show values on graph

Tick the box to include the data values on the graph – these will appear on top of the bar or columns or at each point of the line.

Pie Graphs

There are fewer settings available for pie graphs as only one data field can be plotted on this type of graph. 

Legend Position

Choose a legend position on the graph e.g. on the Left or Right, Top or Bottom. 

Segments

Choose the data field that is going to be represented in the pie by a different colour segment for each data value of the chosen field. 

Segment colours

The colours of the pie graphs segments will be determined automatically by default. The report creator can choose to use a related field to determine the colours if preferred. 

Un-tick the option at the bottom to Determine colours automatically and then tick a field that should be used to colour the segments. Only fields of a “colour” data type will be available for selection and the field can be one that is non-visible on the report data table. 
Show values on graph

Tick the box to include the data values on the graph – these will in the segments of the pie. 

Results Page Layout 

The report creator can design the layout of the report results page incorporating the data table, graphs and formatted text boxes in a variety of positions on the page. 

The layout will be rendered both on screen and on the Download PDF option. 

To design the page layout, click the spanner icon on the report results page and select “Design this page” from the menu. 

The page is divided into Segments, Columns and Objects. 

Add a new segment by scrolling to the bottom of the page and clicking “Add Segment”. 

Each segment can be split into multiple columns by clicking the “Add column” button available when hovering over the right hand side of segment. 

In each column, hover over the right hand side to click the “Add object” button and then select the type of object from the options shown below. 

Drag and drop the objects to move around the page until the desired layout is achieved. 

Click the Done button at the top right of the page to save the page layout design. 

Deleting a Report

A report can be deleted by clicking the spanner icon on the report results page and select “Delete report” from the menu. 

Managing Reports List Page

Clicking on the Report button from an application takes a user to the list of reports that are available to the user. 

To manage the layout and ordering of this page, click the spanner icon from the Reports page and choose the “Design this page” option from the menu. 

Add a new Report Group by clicking the option at the bottom of page. 

Edit the name of an existing group by clicking the “Edit” button within the group. 

Reorder reports within a group by clicking the “Reorder Reports” button. 

Click Done at the top right of the page to save any changes made to the layout of the Report page.

The purpose of the IRIS (Incident Reporting and Investigation System) is to ensure that the University Safety Office can adequately perform its legal obligations to report, document and analyse patterns of accidents and safety related incidents under UK safety legislation.

The Safety Office procured a health and safety management system called InfoExchange, which is produced by Alcumus Group (‘Supplier’). Appendix E: Definitions
All definitions are derived from ITIL (Information Technology Infrastructure Library) publications unless otherwise stated. ITIL is best practice framework for delivering IT Services. 
Change Management:
The process responsible for controlling the lifecycle of all changes, enabling beneficial changes to be made with minimum disruption to IT Services.

Change Types:
Standard: A pre-authorised change that is low risk, relatively common and follows a procedure or work instruction – for example the provision of standard equipment to a new employee.
Normal: Normal changes follow the defined steps of the change management process. Such changes are categorised as Minor, Significant and Major.
Minor: Change is related to a single application and side-effects can be safely excluded.
Significant: Changes affecting several applications, or the whole of major application, or a change affecting fundamental parts of the IT Infrastructure supporting several applications.
Major: Change affecting a major part of the business-critical infrastructure or a change that introduces major new technologies on a considerable scale. 
Emergency Change: A change that must be introduced as soon as possible – for example, to resolve a major incident or implement a security patch.

Change Advisory Board (CAB): A group of people that support the assessment, prioritisation, authorisation and scheduling of changes. A change advisory board is usually made up of representatives from the IT Service Provider; Business Units and on occasion third parties, such as suppliers. The membership of the CAB will reflect the changes being considered.

Customer:
Someone who buys (provides the budget for) goods or Services. The Customer of an IT Service Provider is the person or group who defines and agrees to the Service Level Targets.

Data Retention:
Data retention is the continued storage of an organisation's data for compliance or business reasons. A data retention policy should be created in partnership with the service provider and business unit. It includes a set of guidelines that describes which data will be archived and how long it will be kept for. 

Disaster Recovery:
Disaster recovery (DR) is an area of security planning that aims to protect an organization from the effects of significant negative events. DR allows an organisation to maintain or quickly resume mission-critical functions following a disaster. A disaster recovery plan provides a structured approach for responding to unplanned incidents that threaten a company’s IT infrastructure, including hardware and software, networks, procedures and people.

Incident:
An unplanned interruption to an IT service or reduction in the quality of an IT Service.

IT Service:
A service provided by an IT service provider. An IT Service is made up of a combination of information technology, people and processes.

Process:
A structured set off activities designed to accomplish a specific objective. A process takes one or more defined inputs and turns them into defined outputs.

Recovery Time Objective (RTO):
The maximum time allowed for the recovery of an IT Service following an interruption. The service level to be provided may be less than normal service level targets.

Recovery Point Objective (RPO):
The maximum amount of data that may be lost when service is restored after an interruption. The recovery point objective is expressed as a length of time between the creation/modification of the data and the point of the failure. Data is recovered to the state it was in at the recovery point. Changes after that point are lost.

Request (or Service Request):
A formal request from a user for something to be provided – for example, a request for information or advice; to reset a password; or to install a computer for a new user. Service Requests are managed by the request fulfilment process, usually in conjunction with the service desk.

Service:
A means of delivering value to customers by facilitating outcomes customers want to achieve without the ownership of specific costs and risks.

Service Catalogue:

Stakeholder:
A person who has an interest in an organisation, project or IT Service. Stakeholders may be interested in the activities, targets, resources and deliverables.

Superuser:
A user who is an expert in the business processes supported by an IT service and will provide support for minor incidents and training.

2.1. Service summary 
 
Odyssey is a cloud-based software suite of radiation safety tools designed to assist staff members in managing their 
radiation safety program and increasing compliance. Odyssey is hosted on Amazon Web Services for data security and 
scaling and acts as a centralized location for data entry, storage, and analysis to improve efficiency and reduce cost. 
 
Odyssey software helps staff manage the University’s radiation equipment and materials, and allows for the tracking 
of storage and disposal of radioactive waste. 
 
Odyssey modules include: 
 
 Machine Management 
 Equipment Catalog 
 Inventory Tracking 
 Permits 
 Waste Management 
 Reporting 
 Forms

2.1 Registering a new radiation worker 
An online form will be used to register a new radiation worker, whether they are a student, 
staff or visitor. The form is initiated in the system and will pass through the following stages 
for completion and approval:  
Radiation Worker > RPS > SRPS > Academic Line Manager > Safety Office.  
This form should be used when a radiation worker is registering for the first time in each 
host department. For example, if a worker is already registered with Biology and is now 
registering with Oncology, this form would be used to register the worker as a new worker to 
Oncology.   
In addition, the form should also be used if a worker is registering to work at an external 
institute. 
If the worker is already registered in a Host department but wishes to be registered for a 
different work type or additional radionuclides, then the ‘Work Type Registration’ form 
should be used. (See 3.1 Adding additional work types to a radiation worker record). 
2.1.1 Registration forms have an expiry date to be completed

weeks from the creation date. For example, if the form was sent to the worker on the 
01/08/2024 and the worker selected the link to complete the form after 12/09/2024 they will 
receive an error page and will not be able to complete the registration form.  
If this happens, the SRPS will need to send a new registration form to the worker. Then, the 
Safety Office will be required to Terminate the now expired work registration form.

viewed/completed and the expiration date by navigating to the Link Management Screen; 
Odyssey > Forms > Email Forms > Manage Sent Forms.

workflow to terminate it.

 Introduction
Odyssey is Oxford’s Radiation Management System. A central system to record and manage the University’s radiation-related data including registered workers, materials waste, machines and radiation protection instruments.
All radiation host departments will have access to the system and be required to keep their department records up to date. Only registered radiation workers with an Oxford Single Sign-On (SSO) will have access to the system. 
Note: In the first phase of implementing the system only the Safety Office Radiation Team, Senior Radiation Protection Supervisors (SRPS), and Radiation Protection Supervisors (RPS) will have access to Odyssey. 
Odyssey is a cloud-based system provided by Versant Physics, an American software company. 

 System Configuration
Departments
The EA Environment Agency
The University of Oxford is bound by legislative guidance surrounding the holdings and use of radioactive materials and waste. The legislation is directed through the Environment Agency with a set of Departments that provide the controlling limits for holdings and use of radioactive materials and waste.
The Departments are based on geographical location and are specific to a number of buildings within that location.
Each Department is tailored to the specific activities that take place.
The University of Oxford currently holds the current paper permits.
5 Unsealed Source Permits 
4 Sealed Source Permits 
1 Category 5 Permit
In addition to this the Environment Agency provide an Exemption Order which defines a set of limits for material to be held under exemption conditions. The Exemption Order is applied to each individual building, hence each building has an Exemption Order limit.
Each year, In February, the University of Oxford must provide a return to the EA that describes the full radioactive waste activity for the year. In addition to this, the EA may inspect the University of Oxford and any one of its Permitted locations at any point during the year and require evidence of holdings and use against the limits given to the department, alongside the waste activities.
To amend an EA Permit, an application must be made to the EA for a “Variation”. If successful, the Permit is updated and referenced with a reference suffix at the end of the permit number.
Each Permit is broken down into an agreed set of limits that is given to each Department. This is referred to in the Odyssey system as a “Department Limit”.
The Departments must operate within the limits given to them. Each month they will provide the Safety Office with Source Accountancy Records to confirm their holdings and waste disposal records and to confirm that they remain within their allocated limits.
The source accountancy confirmation and confirmation of waste accumulation and waste disposal to drain and to air will be in the form of a report generated for each department.
Different reports deal with different elements of this process and is further explored in the reporting section below.

Geological Specimens
As at 25/04/2025, Geological Specimens (Rocks) are no longer required to be held under Safeguards regulations.
Rocks contain naturally occurring radionuclides including (but not limited to) Uranium and Thorium. It has been agreed that the University of Oxford will maintain a detailed catalogue of these items in the Digital Asset Management application referred to as EMU. In addition to this, a limited set of data relating to each rock will be kept on the Odyssey system in order to keep track of radiological activity. The two data sets are aligned with a common ID.

In addition, the regulation requires nuclear materials to be reported annually via:

Structure
Structure starts at the University of Oxford level and is based on geographical location. 
The University of Oxford has a number of Departments. 
A Department may be self-contained or may have a number of Sub-Departments. 
Each Department has one or more Buildings. 
Each Building has one or more Rooms, Labs and Waste Stores.
A Department may share a Building with another Department and maintain a set of rooms within the shared building.
A Department may share a Room, Lab or Waste Store within a shared Building with another Department.

 Site Structure

All Departments, Buildings, Rooms, Labs and Waste stores are entities referred to as “Sites”. The University of Oxford will sit at Top Level in the Site Structure and the Departments will sit in the structure underneath this. The Departments all sit as Primary Sites, with the Buildings and Rooms, Labs and Waste Stores shown underneath.
In the example below, the Worker will log into the Pathology Dunn School Department and have visibility to 4 Buildings and have access to 14 Rooms, Labs and Waste Stores.

In the case where a Building is shared, the Building will also be made a Primary Site within the system and must also be given an Association to the Building (See below). This will allow the Workers of both Departments to have visibility of Rooms, Labs and Waste stores to which they have been given access.
In the example below the Worker is located in the JR Hospital Main Building and will log in to either of the Departments RDM Cardiovascular Medicine or Surgical Sciences. This will enable to the Worker to view any of the 4 Rooms/Labs within the JR Hospital Building 622 as defined in their Department limit. 
This is enabled via 2 things.
Through the JR Hospital Main 622 Building being listed as a Primary Site, which sits as a sibling alongside the RDM Cardiovascular Medicine and Surgical Sciences Departments.
Through the creation of an “association” between the Department and the Building.

Associations
To enable visibility of a shared Room, Lab or Waste Store an “Association” needs to be created in the System between the Department and the Shared Building. This is achieved through editing the Department Site (from the Site Structure) and adding an “Association” to the shared Building. Note: please ensure that an “Association” must be created for each Department that shares a Building.
Note: please ensure that the association is created on the Department record and that it cites the Building site. Do not create an association on the Building record citing the Department as this will cause users in both Departments to be able to view the personal details of the other Department through the Worker reporting.

When the Department is created, the Department will dictate exactly what Rooms, Labs, Waste Stores should be visible when using the Department. If the “Association” has been created and the Room, Lab, Waste Store has been added to the Department, the Worker will have visibility of the Room, Lab, Waste Store when logging into the Department on the System.
Please note: 
A lab will only be visible for use with inventory, once it has been set for use with Sealed and/or Unsealed Sources.
A room will only be visible when adding a machine to the system, once it has been set for use with machines.

When logging in to the system, please ensure that you are in the correct Department in which you wish to work. For example, if you wish to “add inventory” to the “Biochemistry Department”, please make sure that you are in the Biochemistry Department.

A user in a Department will see only the Departments and Buildings to which they have an association.

Cardinus Data Import Process (Updated – Automated)
The data import process into Cardinus is now fully automated, replacing the previous manual extraction and processing approach.
Current Process
User data is extracted directly from PeopleXD.
The data is processed and transformed by the University’s Azure team to ensure compatibility with Cardinus.
The processed file is automatically transferred and uploaded to Cardinus via SFTP.
This process runs on a scheduled basis every Wednesday at 4:00am.
Key Features
No manual intervention required: The previous use of Excel processing, and CSV preparation has been retired.
Improved consistency and accuracy: Automated transformation reduces the risk of discrepancies caused by manual handling.
Regular synchronisation: Weekly automated updates ensure that user records are kept up to date.
Data Management Notes
The SSO (format: xxxx1234@ox.ac.uk) remains the unique identifier for users in Cardinus.
Any users present in Cardinus but not included in the latest automated file will continue to be archived automatically.
The process ensures that all active users are maintained, while leavers are appropriately removed. This is of course now reliant on PeopleXD being accurate. 
Process Improvements
Eliminates the need for: 
Manual reconciliation of affiliations and email addresses
Department filtering and validation in Excel
File formatting and concatenation steps
Manual uploads via FileZilla
Reduces risk of large-scale import errors associated with manual processing.
Removes the requirement for the “Pre Cardinus Date” field.
